prompt: The graph of $f$ has two pieces: for $x < -1$ it follows the line $y = 2x + 7$, and for $x \ge -1$ it follows the parabola $y = x^2 + 4$. Find $\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)$.
hint: Two pieces means two one-sided limits. Find each, then see whether they agree.

hints.text: Two pieces means two one-sided limits. Find each, then see whether they agree.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $y = x$ for $x < 1$ and $y = 2 - x$ for $x \ge 1$. Left side heads to $1$, right side to $1$. They agree, so the limit is $1$. Same plan here, with $x = -1$.
Left piece at $x = -1$: $2(-1) + 7$. Right piece at $x = -1$: $(-1)^2 + 4$. Compute both.
Left: $-2 + 7 = 5$. Right: $1 + 4 = 5$. They match, so the limit is $5$.

explanation: From the left, $f$ follows $2x + 7$, which heads to $2(-1) + 7 = 5$.
From the right, $f$ follows $x^2 + 4$, which heads to $(-1)^2 + 4 = 5$.
Both one-sided limits are $5$, so $\lim_{x \to -1} f(x) = 5$. The two pieces join without a jump.

alternativeExplanations.title: Watch the sign trap
steps: A common slip is $(-1)^2 = -1$. Squaring a negative gives a positive: $(-1)^2 = 1$.
So the parabola piece gives $1 + 4 = 5$, not $3$.
With the sign handled, both pieces agree at $5$.
